            <p>contingency plan</p>
            <p>system backup logs or records</p>
            <p>evidence of system backup information transferred to alternate storage site</p>
            <p>alternate storage site agreements</p>
            <p>system security plan</p>
            <p>other relevant documents or records</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="cp-9.5_asm-interview" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="INTERVIEW"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(05)-Interview"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Organizational personnel with system backup responsibilities</p>
            <p>organizational personnel with information security responsibilities</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="cp-9.5_asm-test" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="TEST"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(05)-Test"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Organizational processes for transferring system backups to the alternate storage site</p>
            <p>mechanisms supporting and/or implementing system backups</p>
            <p>mechanisms supporting and/or implementing information transfer to the alternate storage site</p>
          </part>
        </part>
      </control>
      <control class="SP800-53-enhancement" id="cp-9.6">
        <title>Redundant Secondary System</title>
        <prop name="label" class="zero-padded" value="CP-09(06)"/>
        <prop name="label" value="CP-9(6)"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(06)"/>
        <prop name="sort-id" value="cp-09.06"/>
        <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="implementation-level" value="organization"/>
        <link rel="required" href="#cp-9"/>
        <link rel="related" href="#cp-7"/>
        <part name="statement" id="cp-9.6_smt">
          <p>Conduct system backup by maintaining a redundant secondary system that is not collocated with the primary system and that can be activated without loss of information or disruption to operations.</p>
        </part>
        <part name="guidance" id="cp-9.6_gdn">
          <p>The effect of system backup can be achieved by maintaining a redundant secondary system that mirrors the primary system, including the replication of information. If this type of redundancy is in place and there is sufficient geographic separation between the two systems, the secondary system can also serve as the alternate processing site.</p>
        </part>
        <part id="cp-9.6_obj" name="assessment-objective">
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(06)"/>
          <part id="cp-9.6_obj-1" name="assessment-objective">
            <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(06)[01]"/>
            <p>system backup is conducted by maintaining a redundant secondary system that is not collocated with the primary system;</p>
            <link rel="assessment-for" href="#cp-9.6_smt"/>
          </part>
          <part id="cp-9.6_obj-2" name="assessment-objective">
            <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(06)[02]"/>
            <p>system backup is conducted by maintaining a redundant secondary system that can be activated without loss of information or disruption to operations.</p>
            <link rel="assessment-for" href="#cp-9.6_smt"/>
          </part>
          <link rel="assessment-for" href="#cp-9.6_smt"/>
        </part>
        <part id="cp-9.6_asm-examine" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="EXAMINE"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(06)-Examine"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Contingency planning policy</p>
            <p>procedures addressing system backup</p>
            <p>contingency plan</p>
            <p>system backup test results</p>
            <p>contingency plan test results</p>
            <p>contingency plan test documentation</p>
            <p>redundant secondary system for system backups</p>
            <p>location(s) of redundant secondary backup system(s)</p>
            <p>system security plan</p>
            <p>other relevant documents or records</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="cp-9.6_asm-interview" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="INTERVIEW"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(06)-Interview"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Organizational personnel with system backup responsibilities</p>
            <p>organizational personnel with information security responsibilities</p>
            <p>organizational personnel with responsibility for the redundant secondary system</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="cp-9.6_asm-test" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="TEST"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(06)-Test"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Organizational processes for maintaining redundant secondary systems</p>
            <p>mechanisms supporting and/or implementing system backups</p>
            <p>mechanisms supporting and/or implementing information transfer to a redundant secondary system</p>
          </part>
        </part>
      </control>
      <control class="SP800-53-enhancement" id="cp-9.7">
        <title>Dual Authorization for Deletion or Destruction</title>
        <param id="cp-09.07_odp">
          <prop name="alt-identifier" value="cp-9.7_prm_1"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(07)_ODP"/>
          <label>backup information</label>
          <guideline>
            <p>backup information for which to enforce dual authorization in order to delete or destroy is defined;</p>
          </guideline>
        </param>
        <prop name="label" class="zero-padded" value="CP-09(07)"/>
        <prop name="label" value="CP-9(7)"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(07)"/>
        <prop name="sort-id" value="cp-09.07"/>
        <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="implementation-level" value="organization"/>
        <link rel="required" href="#cp-9"/>
        <link rel="related" href="#ac-3"/>
        <link rel="related" href="#ac-5"/>
        <link rel="related" href="#mp-2"/>
        <part name="statement" id="cp-9.7_smt">
          <p>Enforce dual authorization for the deletion or destruction of <insert type="param" id-ref="cp-09.07_odp"/>.</p>
        </part>
        <part name="guidance" id="cp-9.7_gdn">
          <p>Dual authorization ensures that deletion or destruction of backup information cannot occur unless two qualified individuals carry out the task. Individuals deleting or destroying backup information possess the skills or expertise to determine if the proposed deletion or destruction of information reflects organizational policies and procedures. Dual authorization may also be known as two-person control. To reduce the risk of collusion, organizations consider rotating dual authorization duties to other individuals.</p>
        </part>
        <part id="cp-9.7_obj" name="assessment-objective">
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(07)"/>
          <p>dual authorization for the deletion or destruction of <insert type="param" id-ref="cp-09.07_odp"/> is enforced.</p>
          <link rel="assessment-for" href="#cp-9.7_smt"/>
        </part>
        <part id="cp-9.7_asm-examine" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="EXAMINE"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(07)-Examine"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Contingency planning policy</p>
            <p>procedures addressing system backup</p>
            <p>contingency plan</p>
            <p>system design documentation</p>
            <p>system configuration settings and associated documentation</p>
            <p>system generated list of dual authorization credentials or rules</p>
            <p>logs or records of deletion or destruction of backup information</p>
            <p>system security plan</p>
            <p>other relevant documents or records</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="cp-9.7_asm-interview" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="INTERVIEW"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(07)-Interview"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Organizational personnel with system backup responsibilities</p>
            <p>organizational personnel with information security responsibilities</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="cp-9.7_asm-test" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="TEST"/>

            <p>Mechanisms supporting and/or implementing dual authorization</p>
            <p>mechanisms supporting and/or implementing the deletion/destruction of backup information</p>
          </part>
        </part>
      </control>
      <control class="SP800-53-enhancement" id="cp-9.8">
        <title>Cryptographic Protection</title>
        <param id="cp-09.08_odp">
          <prop name="alt-identifier" value="cp-9.8_prm_1"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(08)_ODP"/>
          <label>backup information</label>
          <guideline>
            <p>backup information to protect against unauthorized disclosure and modification is defined;</p>
          </guideline>
        </param>
        <prop name="label" class="zero-padded" value="CP-09(08)"/>
        <prop name="label" value="CP-9(8)"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(08)"/>
        <prop name="sort-id" value="cp-09.08"/>
        <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="implementation-level" value="organization"/>
        <link rel="required" href="#cp-9"/>
        <link rel="related" href="#sc-12"/>
        <link rel="related" href="#sc-13"/>
        <link rel="related" href="#sc-28"/>
        <part name="statement" id="cp-9.8_smt">
          <p>Implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure and modification of <insert type="param" id-ref="cp-09.08_odp"/>.</p>
        </part>
        <part name="guidance" id="cp-9.8_gdn">
          <p>The selection of cryptographic mechanisms is based on the need to protect the confidentiality and integrity of backup information. The strength of mechanisms selected is commensurate with the security category or classification of the information. Cryptographic protection applies to system backup information in storage at both primary and alternate locations. Organizations that implement cryptographic mechanisms to protect information at rest also consider cryptographic key management solutions.</p>
        </part>
        <part id="cp-9.8_obj" name="assessment-objective">
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(08)"/>
          <p>cryptographic mechanisms are implemented to prevent unauthorized disclosure and modification of <insert type="param" id-ref="cp-09.08_odp"/>.</p>
          <link rel="assessment-for" href="#cp-9.8_smt"/>
        </part>
        <part id="cp-9.8_asm-examine" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="EXAMINE"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(08)-Examine"/>

            <p>Contingency planning policy</p>
            <p>procedures addressing system backup</p>
            <p>contingency plan</p>
            <p>system design documentation</p>
            <p>system configuration settings and associated documentation</p>
            <p>system security plan</p>
            <p>other relevant documents or records</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="cp-9.8_asm-interview" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="INTERVIEW"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(08)-Interview"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Organizational personnel with system backup responsibilities</p>
            <p>organizational personnel with information security responsibilities</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="cp-9.8_asm-test" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="TEST"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-09(08)-Test"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Mechanisms supporting and/or implementing cryptographic protection of backup information</p>
          </part>
        </part>
      </control>
    </control>
    <control class="SP800-53" id="cp-10">
      <title>System Recovery and Reconstitution</title>
      <param id="cp-10_prm_1">
        <prop name="aggregates" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="cp-10_odp.01"/>
        <prop name="aggregates" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="cp-10_odp.02"/>
        <label>organization-defined time period consistent with recovery time and recovery point objectives</label>
      </param>
      <param id="cp-10_odp.01">
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-10_ODP[01]"/>
        <label>time period</label>
        <guideline>
          <p>time period consistent with recovery time and recovery point objectives for the recovery of the system is determined;</p>
        </guideline>
      </param>
      <param id="cp-10_odp.02">
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-10_ODP[02]"/>
        <label>time period</label>
        <guideline>
          <p>time period consistent with recovery time and recovery point objectives for the reconstitution of the system is determined;</p>
        </guideline>
      </param>
      <prop name="label" class="zero-padded" value="CP-10"/>
        <prop name="label" value="CP-10"/>
      <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-10"/>
      <prop name="sort-id" value="cp-10"/>
      <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="implementation-level" value="organization"/>
      <link rel="reference" href="#bc39f179-c735-4da2-b7a7-b2b622119755"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#cp-2"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#cp-4"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#cp-6"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#cp-7"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#cp-9"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#ir-4"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#sa-8"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#sc-24"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#si-13"/>
      <part name="statement" id="cp-10_smt">
        <p>Provide for the recovery and reconstitution of the system to a known state within <insert type="param" id-ref="cp-10_prm_1"/> after a disruption, compromise, or failure.</p>
      </part>
      <part name="guidance" id="cp-10_gdn">
        <p>Recovery is executing contingency plan activities to restore organizational mission and business functions. Reconstitution takes place following recovery and includes activities for returning systems to fully operational states. Recovery and reconstitution operations reflect mission and business priorities; recovery point, recovery time, and reconstitution objectives; and organizational metrics consistent with contingency plan requirements. Reconstitution includes the deactivation of interim system capabilities that may have been needed during recovery operations. Reconstitution also includes assessments of fully restored system capabilities, reestablishment of continuous monitoring activities, system reauthorization (if required), and activities to prepare the system and organization for future disruptions, breaches, compromises, or failures. Recovery and reconstitution capabilities can include automated mechanisms and manual procedures. Organizations establish recovery time and recovery point objectives as part of contingency planning.</p>
      </part>
      <part id="cp-10_obj" name="assessment-objective">
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-10"/>
        <part id="cp-10_obj-1" name="assessment-objective">
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-10[01]"/>
          <p>the recovery of the system to a known state is provided within <insert type="param" id-ref="cp-10_odp.01"/> after a disruption, compromise, or failure;</p>
          <link rel="assessment-for" href="#cp-10_smt"/>
        </part>
        <part id="cp-10_obj-2" name="assessment-objective">
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-10[02]"/>
          <p>a reconstitution of the system to a known state is provided within <insert type="param" id-ref="cp-10_odp.02"/> after a disruption, compromise, or failure.</p>
          <link rel="assessment-for" href="#cp-10_smt"/>
        </part>
        <link rel="assessment-for" href="#cp-10_smt"/>
      </part>
      <part id="cp-10_asm-examine" name="assessment-method">
        <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="EXAMINE"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-10-Examine"/>
        <part name="assessment-objects">
          <p>Contingency planning policy</p>
          <p>procedures addressing system backup</p>
          <p>contingency plan</p>
          <p>system backup test results</p>
          <p>contingency plan test results</p>
          <p>contingency plan test documentation</p>
          <p>redundant secondary system for system backups</p>
          <p>location(s) of redundant secondary backup system(s)</p>
          <p>system security plan</p>
          <p>other relevant documents or records</p>
        </part>
      </part>
      <part id="cp-10_asm-interview" name="assessment-method">
        <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="INTERVIEW"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-10-Interview"/>
        <part name="assessment-objects">
          <p>Organizational personnel with contingency planning, recovery, and/or reconstitution responsibilities</p>
          <p>organizational personnel with information security responsibilities</p>
        </part>
      </part>
      <part id="cp-10_asm-test" name="assessment-method">
        <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="TEST"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-10-Test"/>
        <part name="assessment-objects">
          <p>Organizational processes implementing system recovery and reconstitution operations</p>
          <p>mechanisms supporting and/or implementing system recovery and reconstitution operations</p>
        </part>
      </part>

          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="TEST"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-10(02)-Test"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Mechanisms supporting and/or implementing transaction recovery capability</p>
          </part>
        </part>
      </control>

        <prop name="label" value="CP-10(3)"/>

          <p>alternative communications protocols in support of maintaining continuity of operations are defined;</p>
        </guideline>

      <part name="statement" id="cp-11_smt">
        <p>Provide the capability to employ <insert type="param" id-ref="cp-11_odp"/> in support of maintaining continuity of operations.</p>
      </part>
      <part name="guidance" id="cp-11_gdn">
        <p>Contingency plans and the contingency training or testing associated with those plans incorporate an alternate communications protocol capability as part of establishing resilience in organizational systems. Switching communications protocols may affect software applications and operational aspects of systems. Organizations assess the potential side effects of introducing alternate communications protocols prior to implementation.</p>
      </part>

        <link rel="assessment-for" href="#cp-11_smt"/>
      </part>

          <p>system configuration settings and associated documentation</p>
          <p>list of alternative communications protocols supporting continuity of operations</p>
          <p>system security plan</p>
          <p>other relevant documents or records</p>
        </part>

          <p>organizational personnel with continuity of operations planning and plan implementation responsibilities</p>
          <p>organizational personnel with information security responsibilities</p>
          <p>system/network administrators</p>
          <p>system developers</p>
        </part>
      </part>
      <part id="cp-11_asm-test" name="assessment-method">
        <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="TEST"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-11-Test"/>
        <part name="assessment-objects">
          <p>Mechanisms employing alternative communications protocols</p>
        </part>

      <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-12"/>
      <prop name="sort-id" value="cp-12"/>
      <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="implementation-level" value="system"/>
      <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="contributes-to-assurance" value="true"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#cm-2"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#sa-8"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#sc-24"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#si-13"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#si-17"/>
      <part name="statement" id="cp-12_smt">
        <p>When <insert type="param" id-ref="cp-12_odp.02"/> are detected, enter a safe mode of operation with <insert type="param" id-ref="cp-12_odp.01"/>.</p>
      </part>
      <part name="guidance" id="cp-12_gdn">
        <p>For systems that support critical mission and business functions—including military operations, civilian space operations, nuclear power plant operations, and air traffic control operations (especially real-time operational environments)—organizations can identify certain conditions under which those systems revert to a predefined safe mode of operation. The safe mode of operation, which can be activated either automatically or manually, restricts the operations that systems can execute when those conditions are encountered. Restriction includes allowing only selected functions to execute that can be carried out under limited power or with reduced communications bandwidth.</p>
      </part>
      <part id="cp-12_obj" name="assessment-objective">
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-12"/>
        <p>a safe mode of operation is entered with <insert type="param" id-ref="cp-12_odp.01"/> when <insert type="param" id-ref="cp-12_odp.02"/> are detected.</p>
        <link rel="assessment-for" href="#cp-12_smt"/>
      </part>
      <part id="cp-12_asm-examine" name="assessment-method">
        <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="EXAMINE"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-12-Examine"/>
        <part name="assessment-objects">
          <p>Contingency planning policy</p>
          <p>procedures addressing safe mode of operation for the system</p>
          <p>contingency plan</p>
          <p>system design documentation</p>
          <p>system configuration settings and associated documentation</p>
          <p>system administration manuals</p>
          <p>system operation manuals</p>
          <p>system installation manuals</p>
          <p>contingency plan test records</p>
          <p>incident handling records</p>
          <p>system audit records</p>
          <p>system security plan</p>
          <p>other relevant documents or records</p>
        </part>
      </part>
      <part id="cp-12_asm-interview" name="assessment-method">
        <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="INTERVIEW"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-12-Interview"/>
        <part name="assessment-objects">
          <p>Organizational personnel with system operation responsibilities</p>
          <p>organizational personnel with information security responsibilities</p>
          <p>system/network administrators</p>
          <p>system developers</p>
        </part>
      </part>
      <part id="cp-12_asm-test" name="assessment-method">
        <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="TEST"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-12-Test"/>

          <p>Mechanisms implementing safe mode of operation</p>
        </part>

    <control class="SP800-53" id="cp-13">
      <title>Alternative Security Mechanisms</title>
      <param id="cp-13_odp.01">
        <prop name="alt-identifier" value="cp-13_prm_1"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-13_ODP[01]"/>
        <label>alternative or supplemental security mechanisms</label>
        <guideline>
          <p>alternative or supplemental security mechanisms are defined;</p>
        </guideline>
      </param>
      <param id="cp-13_odp.02">
        <prop name="alt-identifier" value="cp-13_prm_2"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-13_ODP[02]"/>
        <label>security functions</label>
        <guideline>
          <p>security functions are defined;</p>
        </guideline>
      </param>
      <prop name="label" class="zero-padded" value="CP-13"/>
        <prop name="label" value="CP-13"/>
      <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-13"/>
      <prop name="sort-id" value="cp-13"/>
      <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="implementation-level" value="organization"/>
      <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="implementation-level" value="system"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#cp-2"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#cp-11"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#si-13"/>
      <part name="statement" id="cp-13_smt">
        <p>Employ <insert type="param" id-ref="cp-13_odp.01"/> for satisfying <insert type="param" id-ref="cp-13_odp.02"/> when the primary means of implementing the security function is unavailable or compromised.</p>
      </part>
      <part name="guidance" id="cp-13_gdn">
        <p>Use of alternative security mechanisms supports system resiliency, contingency planning, and continuity of operations. To ensure mission and business continuity, organizations can implement alternative or supplemental security mechanisms. The mechanisms may be less effective than the primary mechanisms. However, having the capability to readily employ alternative or supplemental mechanisms enhances mission and business continuity that might otherwise be adversely impacted if operations had to be curtailed until the primary means of implementing the functions was restored. Given the cost and level of effort required to provide such alternative capabilities, the alternative or supplemental mechanisms are only applied to critical security capabilities provided by systems, system components, or system services. For example, an organization may issue one-time pads to senior executives, officials, and system administrators if multi-factor tokens—the standard means for achieving secure authentication— are compromised.</p>
      </part>
      <part id="cp-13_obj" name="assessment-objective">
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-13"/>
        <p><insert type="param" id-ref="cp-13_odp.01"/> are employed for satisfying <insert type="param" id-ref="cp-13_odp.02"/> when the primary means of implementing the security function is unavailable or compromised.</p>
        <link rel="assessment-for" href="#cp-13_smt"/>
      </part>
      <part id="cp-13_asm-examine" name="assessment-method">
        <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="EXAMINE"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-13-Examine"/>
        <part name="assessment-objects">
          <p>Contingency planning policy</p>
          <p>procedures addressing alternate security mechanisms</p>
          <p>contingency plan</p>
          <p>continuity of operations plan</p>
          <p>system design documentation</p>
          <p>system configuration settings and associated documentation</p>
          <p>contingency plan test records</p>
          <p>contingency plan test results</p>
          <p>system security plan</p>
          <p>other relevant documents or records</p>
        </part>
      </part>
      <part id="cp-13_asm-interview" name="assessment-method">
        <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="INTERVIEW"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-13-Interview"/>
        <part name="assessment-objects">
          <p>Organizational personnel with system operation responsibilities</p>
          <p>organizational personnel with information security responsibilities</p>
        </part>
      </part>
      <part id="cp-13_asm-test" name="assessment-method">
        <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="TEST"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="CP-13-Test"/>
        <part name="assessment-objects">
          <p>system capability implementing alternative security mechanisms</p>
        </part>
      </part>

      <link rel="reference" href="#27847491-5ce1-4f6a-a1e4-9e483782f0ef"/>

      <link rel="reference" href="#c7ac44e8-10db-4b64-b2b9-9e32ec1efed0"/>

      <part name="statement" id="ia-1_smt">
        <part name="item" id="ia-1_smt.a">
          <prop name="label" value="a."/>
          <p>Develop, document, and disseminate to <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-1_prm_1"/>:</p>
          <part name="item" id="ia-1_smt.a.1">
            <prop name="label" value="1."/>
            <p><insert type="param" id-ref="ia-01_odp.03"/> identification and authentication policy that:</p>
            <part name="item" id="ia-1_smt.a.1.a">
              <prop name="label" value="(a)"/>
              <p>Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and</p>
            </part>
            <part name="item" id="ia-1_smt.a.1.b">
              <prop name="label" value="(b)"/>
              <p>Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and</p>
            </part>
          </part>
          <part name="item" id="ia-1_smt.a.2">
            <prop name="label" value="2."/>
            <p>Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the identification and authentication policy and the associated identification and authentication controls;</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part name="item" id="ia-1_smt.b">
          <prop name="label" value="b."/>
          <p>Designate an <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-01_odp.04"/> to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the identification and authentication policy and procedures; and</p>
        </part>
        <part name="item" id="ia-1_smt.c">
          <prop name="label" value="c."/>
          <p>Review and update the current identification and authentication:</p>
          <part name="item" id="ia-1_smt.c.1">
            <prop name="label" value="1."/>
            <p>Policy <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-01_odp.05"/> and following <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-01_odp.06"/> ; and</p>
          </part>
          <part name="item" id="ia-1_smt.c.2">
            <prop name="label" value="2."/>
            <p>Procedures <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-01_odp.07"/> and following <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-01_odp.08"/>.</p>
          </part>
        </part>
      </part>
      <part name="guidance" id="ia-1_gdn">
        <p>Identification and authentication policy and procedures address the controls in the IA family that are implemented within systems and organizations. The risk management strategy is an important factor in establishing such policies and procedures. Policies and procedures contribute to security and privacy assurance. Therefore, it is important that security and privacy programs collaborate on the development of identification and authentication policy and procedures. Security and privacy program policies and procedures at the organization level are preferable, in general, and may obviate the need for mission- or system-specific policies and procedures. The policy can be included as part of the general security and privacy policy or be represented by multiple policies that reflect the complex nature of organizations. Procedures can be established for security and privacy programs, for mission or business processes, and for systems, if needed. Procedures describe how the policies or controls are implemented and can be directed at the individual or role that is the object of the procedure. Procedures can be documented in system security and privacy plans or in one or more separate documents. Events that may precipitate an update to identification and authentication policy and procedures include assessment or audit findings, security incidents or breaches, or changes in applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines. Simply restating controls does not constitute an organizational policy or procedure.</p>
      </part>

    <control class="SP800-53" id="ia-2">
      <title>Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)</title>
      <prop name="label" class="zero-padded" value="IA-02"/>

      <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="implementation-level" value="system"/>
      <link rel="reference" href="#678e3d6c-150b-4393-aec5-6e3481eb1e00"/>
      <link rel="reference" href="#7ba1d91c-3934-4d5a-8532-b32f864ad34c"/>

      <part name="statement" id="ia-2_smt">
        <p>Uniquely identify and authenticate organizational users and associate that unique identification with processes acting on behalf of those users.</p>
      </part>
      <part name="guidance" id="ia-2_gdn">
        <p>Organizations can satisfy the identification and authentication requirements by complying with the requirements in <a href="#f16e438e-7114-4144-bfe2-2dfcad8cb2d0">HSPD 12</a> . Organizational users include employees or individuals who organizations consider to have an equivalent status to employees (e.g., contractors and guest researchers). Unique identification and authentication of users applies to all accesses other than those that are explicitly identified in <a href="#ac-14">AC-14</a> and that occur through the authorized use of group authenticators without individual authentication. Since processes execute on behalf of groups and roles, organizations may require unique identification of individuals in group accounts or for detailed accountability of individual activity.</p>
        <p>Organizations employ passwords, physical authenticators, or biometrics to authenticate user identities or, in the case of multi-factor authentication, some combination thereof. Access to organizational systems is defined as either local access or network access. Local access is any access to organizational systems by users or processes acting on behalf of users, where access is obtained through direct connections without the use of networks. Network access is access to organizational systems by users (or processes acting on behalf of users) where access is obtained through network connections (i.e., nonlocal accesses). Remote access is a type of network access that involves communication through external networks. Internal networks include local area networks and wide area networks.</p>
        <p>The use of encrypted virtual private networks for network connections between organization-controlled endpoints and non-organization-controlled endpoints may be treated as internal networks with respect to protecting the confidentiality and integrity of information traversing the network. Identification and authentication requirements for non-organizational users are described in <a href="#ia-8">IA-8</a>.</p>
      </part>
      <part id="ia-2_obj" name="assessment-objective">
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02"/>
        <part id="ia-2_obj-1" name="assessment-objective">
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02[01]"/>
          <p>organizational users are uniquely identified and authenticated;</p>
          <link rel="assessment-for" href="#ia-2_smt"/>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2_obj-2" name="assessment-objective">
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02[02]"/>
          <p>the unique identification of authenticated organizational users is associated with processes acting on behalf of those users.</p>
          <link rel="assessment-for" href="#ia-2_smt"/>
        </part>
        <link rel="assessment-for" href="#ia-2_smt"/>
      </part>
      <part id="ia-2_asm-examine" name="assessment-method">
        <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="EXAMINE"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02-Examine"/>
        <part name="assessment-objects">

          <p>procedures addressing user identification and authentication</p>
          <p>system security plan, system design documentation</p>
          <p>system configuration settings and associated documentation</p>
          <p>system audit records</p>
          <p>list of system accounts</p>
          <p>other relevant documents or records</p>
        </part>
      </part>
      <part id="ia-2_asm-interview" name="assessment-method">
        <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="INTERVIEW"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02-Interview"/>
        <part name="assessment-objects">
          <p>Organizational personnel with system operations responsibilities</p>
          <p>organizational personnel with information security responsibilities</p>
          <p>system/network administrators</p>
          <p>organizational personnel with account management responsibilities</p>
          <p>system developers</p>
        </part>
      </part>
      <part id="ia-2_asm-test" name="assessment-method">
        <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="TEST"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02-Test"/>
        <part name="assessment-objects">
          <p>Organizational processes for uniquely identifying and authenticating users</p>
          <p>mechanisms supporting and/or implementing identification and authentication capabilities</p>
        </part>
      </part>
      <control class="SP800-53-enhancement" id="ia-2.1">
        <title>Multi-factor Authentication to Privileged Accounts</title>
        <prop name="label" class="zero-padded" value="IA-02(01)"/>
        <prop name="label" value="IA-2(1)"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(01)"/>
        <prop name="sort-id" value="ia-02.01"/>
        <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="implementation-level" value="system"/>
        <link rel="required" href="#ia-2"/>
        <link rel="related" href="#ac-5"/>
        <link rel="related" href="#ac-6"/>
        <part name="statement" id="ia-2.1_smt">
          <p>Implement multi-factor authentication for access to privileged accounts.</p>
        </part>
        <part name="guidance" id="ia-2.1_gdn">
          <p>Multi-factor authentication requires the use of two or more different factors to achieve authentication. The authentication factors are defined as follows: something you know (e.g., a personal identification number [PIN]), something you have (e.g., a physical authenticator such as a cryptographic private key), or something you are (e.g., a biometric). Multi-factor authentication solutions that feature physical authenticators include hardware authenticators that provide time-based or challenge-response outputs and smart cards such as the U.S. Government Personal Identity Verification (PIV) card or the Department of Defense (DoD) Common Access Card (CAC). In addition to authenticating users at the system level (i.e., at logon), organizations may employ authentication mechanisms at the application level, at their discretion, to provide increased security. Regardless of the type of access (i.e., local, network, remote), privileged accounts are authenticated using multi-factor options appropriate for the level of risk. Organizations can add additional security measures, such as additional or more rigorous authentication mechanisms, for specific types of access.</p>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.1_obj" name="assessment-objective">
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(01)"/>
          <p>multi-factor authentication is implemented for access to privileged accounts.</p>
          <link rel="assessment-for" href="#ia-2.1_smt"/>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.1_asm-examine" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="EXAMINE"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(01)-Examine"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Identification and authentication policy</p>
            <p>procedures addressing user identification and authentication</p>
            <p>system security plan</p>
            <p>system design documentation</p>
            <p>system configuration settings and associated documentation</p>
            <p>system audit records</p>
            <p>list of system accounts</p>
            <p>other relevant documents or records</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.1_asm-interview" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="INTERVIEW"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(01)-Interview"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Organizational personnel with system operations responsibilities</p>
            <p>organizational personnel with account management responsibilities</p>
            <p>organizational personnel with information security responsibilities</p>
            <p>system/network administrators</p>
            <p>system developers</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.1_asm-test" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="TEST"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(01)-Test"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Mechanisms supporting and/or implementing a multi-factor authentication capability</p>
          </part>
        </part>
      </control>
      <control class="SP800-53-enhancement" id="ia-2.2">
        <title>Multi-factor Authentication to Non-privileged Accounts</title>
        <prop name="label" class="zero-padded" value="IA-02(02)"/>
        <prop name="label" value="IA-2(2)"/>

        <part name="statement" id="ia-2.2_smt">
          <p>Implement multi-factor authentication for access to non-privileged accounts.</p>
        </part>
        <part name="guidance" id="ia-2.2_gdn">
          <p>Multi-factor authentication requires the use of two or more different factors to achieve authentication. The authentication factors are defined as follows: something you know (e.g., a personal identification number [PIN]), something you have (e.g., a physical authenticator such as a cryptographic private key), or something you are (e.g., a biometric). Multi-factor authentication solutions that feature physical authenticators include hardware authenticators that provide time-based or challenge-response outputs and smart cards such as the U.S. Government Personal Identity Verification card or the DoD Common Access Card. In addition to authenticating users at the system level, organizations may also employ authentication mechanisms at the application level, at their discretion, to provide increased information security. Regardless of the type of access (i.e., local, network, remote), non-privileged accounts are authenticated using multi-factor options appropriate for the level of risk. Organizations can provide additional security measures, such as additional or more rigorous authentication mechanisms, for specific types of access.</p>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.2_obj" name="assessment-objective">
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(02)"/>
          <p>multi-factor authentication for access to non-privileged accounts is implemented.</p>
          <link rel="assessment-for" href="#ia-2.2_smt"/>

      <control class="SP800-53-enhancement" id="ia-2.5">
        <title>Individual Authentication with Group Authentication</title>
        <prop name="label" class="zero-padded" value="IA-02(05)"/>
        <prop name="label" value="IA-2(5)"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(05)"/>
        <prop name="sort-id" value="ia-02.05"/>
        <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="implementation-level" value="organization"/>
        <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="implementation-level" value="system"/>
        <link rel="required" href="#ia-2"/>
        <part name="statement" id="ia-2.5_smt">
          <p>When shared accounts or authenticators are employed, require users to be individually authenticated before granting access to the shared accounts or resources.</p>
        </part>
        <part name="guidance" id="ia-2.5_gdn">
          <p>Individual authentication prior to shared group authentication mitigates the risk of using group accounts or authenticators.</p>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.5_obj" name="assessment-objective">
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(05)"/>
          <p>users are required to be individually authenticated before granting access to the shared accounts or resources when shared accounts or authenticators are employed.</p>
          <link rel="assessment-for" href="#ia-2.5_smt"/>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.5_asm-examine" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="EXAMINE"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(05)-Examine"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">

            <p>system security plan</p>

      <control class="SP800-53-enhancement" id="ia-2.6">
        <title>Access to Accounts —separate Device</title>
        <param id="ia-02.06_odp.01">
          <prop name="alt-identifier" value="ia-2.6_prm_1"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(06)_ODP[01]"/>
          <select how-many="one-or-more">
            <choice>local</choice>
            <choice>network</choice>
            <choice>remote</choice>
          </select>
        </param>
        <param id="ia-02.06_odp.02">
          <prop name="alt-identifier" value="ia-2.6_prm_2"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(06)_ODP[02]"/>
          <select how-many="one-or-more">
            <choice>privileged accounts</choice>
            <choice>non-privileged accounts</choice>
          </select>
        </param>
        <param id="ia-02.06_odp.03">
          <prop name="alt-identifier" value="ia-2.6_prm_3"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(06)_ODP[03]"/>
          <label>strength of mechanism requirements</label>
          <guideline>
            <p>the strength of mechanism requirements to be enforced by a device separate from the system gaining access to accounts is defined;</p>
          </guideline>
        </param>
        <prop name="label" class="zero-padded" value="IA-02(06)"/>
        <prop name="label" value="IA-2(6)"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(06)"/>
        <prop name="sort-id" value="ia-02.06"/>
        <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="implementation-level" value="system"/>
        <link rel="required" href="#ia-2"/>
        <link rel="related" href="#ac-6"/>
        <part name="statement" id="ia-2.6_smt">
          <p>Implement multi-factor authentication for <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-02.06_odp.01"/> access to <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-02.06_odp.02"/> such that:</p>
          <part name="item" id="ia-2.6_smt.a">
            <prop name="label" value="(a)"/>
            <p>One of the factors is provided by a device separate from the system gaining access; and</p>
          </part>
          <part name="item" id="ia-2.6_smt.b">
            <prop name="label" value="(b)"/>
            <p>The device meets <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-02.06_odp.03"/>.</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part name="guidance" id="ia-2.6_gdn">
          <p>The purpose of requiring a device that is separate from the system to which the user is attempting to gain access for one of the factors during multi-factor authentication is to reduce the likelihood of compromising authenticators or credentials stored on the system. Adversaries may be able to compromise such authenticators or credentials and subsequently impersonate authorized users. Implementing one of the factors on a separate device (e.g., a hardware token), provides a greater strength of mechanism and an increased level of assurance in the authentication process.</p>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.6_obj" name="assessment-objective">
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(06)"/>
          <part id="ia-2.6_obj.a" name="assessment-objective">
            <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(06)(a)"/>
            <p>multi-factor authentication is implemented for <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-02.06_odp.01"/> access to <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-02.06_odp.02"/> such that one of the factors is provided by a device separate from the system gaining access;</p>
            <link rel="assessment-for" href="#ia-2.6_smt.a"/>
          </part>
          <part id="ia-2.6_obj.b" name="assessment-objective">
            <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(06)(b)"/>
            <p>multi-factor authentication is implemented for <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-02.06_odp.01"/> access to <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-02.06_odp.02"/> such that the device meets <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-02.06_odp.03"/>.</p>
            <link rel="assessment-for" href="#ia-2.6_smt.b"/>
          </part>
          <link rel="assessment-for" href="#ia-2.6_smt"/>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.6_asm-examine" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="EXAMINE"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(06)-Examine"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">

            <p>list of system accounts</p>
            <p>other relevant documents or records</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.6_asm-interview" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="INTERVIEW"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(06)-Interview"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Organizational personnel with system operations responsibilities</p>
            <p>organizational personnel with account management responsibilities</p>
            <p>organizational personnel with information security responsibilities</p>
            <p>system/network administrators</p>
            <p>system developers</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.6_asm-test" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="TEST"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(06)-Test"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Mechanisms supporting and/or implementing multi-factor authentication capability</p>
          </part>
        </part>
      </control>

        <link rel="incorporated-into" href="#ia-2.6"/>

      <control class="SP800-53-enhancement" id="ia-2.8">
        <title>Access to Accounts — Replay Resistant</title>
        <param id="ia-02.08_odp">
          <prop name="alt-identifier" value="ia-2.8_prm_1"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(08)_ODP"/>
          <select how-many="one-or-more">
            <choice>privileged accounts</choice>
            <choice>non-privileged accounts</choice>
          </select>
        </param>
        <prop name="label" class="zero-padded" value="IA-02(08)"/>
        <prop name="label" value="IA-2(8)"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(08)"/>
        <prop name="sort-id" value="ia-02.08"/>
        <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="implementation-level" value="system"/>
        <link rel="required" href="#ia-2"/>
        <part name="statement" id="ia-2.8_smt">
          <p>Implement replay-resistant authentication mechanisms for access to <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-02.08_odp"/>.</p>
        </part>
        <part name="guidance" id="ia-2.8_gdn">
          <p>Authentication processes resist replay attacks if it is impractical to achieve successful authentications by replaying previous authentication messages. Replay-resistant techniques include protocols that use nonces or challenges such as time synchronous or cryptographic authenticators.</p>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.8_obj" name="assessment-objective">
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(08)"/>
          <p>replay-resistant authentication mechanisms for access to <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-02.08_odp"/> are implemented.</p>
          <link rel="assessment-for" href="#ia-2.8_smt"/>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.8_asm-examine" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="EXAMINE"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(08)-Examine"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Identification and authentication policy</p>
            <p>system security plan</p>
            <p>procedures addressing user identification and authentication</p>
            <p>system design documentation</p>
            <p>system configuration settings and associated documentation</p>
            <p>system audit records</p>
            <p>list of privileged system accounts</p>
            <p>other relevant documents or records</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.8_asm-interview" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="INTERVIEW"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(08)-Interview"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Organizational personnel with system operations responsibilities</p>
            <p>organizational personnel with account management responsibilities</p>
            <p>organizational personnel with information security responsibilities</p>
            <p>system/network administrators</p>
            <p>system developers</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.8_asm-test" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="TEST"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(08)-Test"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Mechanisms supporting and/or implementing identification and authentication capabilities</p>
            <p>Mechanisms supporting and/or implementing replay-resistant authentication mechanisms</p>
          </part>
        </part>
      </control>
      <control class="SP800-53-enhancement" id="ia-2.9">
        <title>Network Access to Non-privileged Accounts — Replay Resistant</title>
        <prop name="label" class="zero-padded" value="IA-02(09)"/>
        <prop name="label" value="IA-2(9)"/>

      <control class="SP800-53-enhancement" id="ia-2.10">
        <title>Single Sign-on</title>
        <param id="ia-02.10_odp">
          <prop name="alt-identifier" value="ia-2.10_prm_1"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(10)_ODP"/>
          <label>system accounts and services</label>
          <guideline>
            <p>system accounts and services for which a single sign-on capability must be provided are defined;</p>
          </guideline>
        </param>
        <prop name="label" class="zero-padded" value="IA-02(10)"/>
        <prop name="label" value="IA-2(10)"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(10)"/>
        <prop name="sort-id" value="ia-02.10"/>
        <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="implementation-level" value="system"/>
        <link rel="required" href="#ia-2"/>
        <part name="statement" id="ia-2.10_smt">
          <p>Provide a single sign-on capability for <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-02.10_odp"/>.</p>
        </part>
        <part name="guidance" id="ia-2.10_gdn">
          <p>Single sign-on enables users to log in once and gain access to multiple system resources. Organizations consider the operational efficiencies provided by single sign-on capabilities with the risk introduced by allowing access to multiple systems via a single authentication event. Single sign-on can present opportunities to improve system security, for example by providing the ability to add multi-factor authentication for applications and systems (existing and new) that may not be able to natively support multi-factor authentication.</p>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.10_obj" name="assessment-objective">
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(10)"/>
          <p>a single sign-on capability is provided for <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-02.10_odp"/>.</p>
          <link rel="assessment-for" href="#ia-2.10_smt"/>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.10_asm-examine" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="EXAMINE"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(10)-Examine"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Identification and authentication policy</p>
            <p>system security plan</p>
            <p>procedures addressing single sign-on capability for system accounts and services</p>
            <p>procedures addressing identification and authentication</p>
            <p>system design documentation</p>
            <p>system configuration settings and associated documentation</p>
            <p>system audit records</p>
            <p>list of system accounts and services requiring single sign-on capability</p>
            <p>other relevant documents or records</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.10_asm-interview" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="INTERVIEW"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(10)-Interview"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Organizational personnel with system operations responsibilities</p>
            <p>organizational personnel with account management responsibilities</p>
            <p>organizational personnel with information security responsibilities</p>
            <p>system/network administrators</p>
            <p>system developers</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.10_asm-test" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="TEST"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(10)-Test"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Mechanisms supporting and/or implementing identification and authentication capabilities</p>
            <p>mechanisms supporting and/or implementing single sign-on capability for system accounts and services</p>
          </part>
        </part>
      </control>
      <control class="SP800-53-enhancement" id="ia-2.11">

        <prop name="label" class="zero-padded" value="IA-02(11)"/>

      <control class="SP800-53-enhancement" id="ia-2.12">
        <title>Acceptance of PIV Credentials</title>
        <prop name="label" class="zero-padded" value="IA-02(12)"/>
        <prop name="label" value="IA-2(12)"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(12)"/>
        <prop name="sort-id" value="ia-02.12"/>
        <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="implementation-level" value="system"/>
        <link rel="required" href="#ia-2"/>
        <part name="statement" id="ia-2.12_smt">
          <p>Accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification-compliant credentials.</p>
        </part>
        <part name="guidance" id="ia-2.12_gdn">
          <p>Acceptance of Personal Identity Verification (PIV)-compliant credentials applies to organizations implementing logical access control and physical access control systems. PIV-compliant credentials are those credentials issued by federal agencies that conform to FIPS Publication 201 and supporting guidance documents. The adequacy and reliability of PIV card issuers are authorized using <a href="#10963761-58fc-4b20-b3d6-b44a54daba03">SP 800-79-2</a> . Acceptance of PIV-compliant credentials includes derived PIV credentials, the use of which is addressed in <a href="#e8552d48-cf41-40aa-8b06-f45f7fb4706c">SP 800-166</a> . The DOD Common Access Card (CAC) is an example of a PIV credential.</p>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.12_obj" name="assessment-objective">
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(12)"/>
          <p>Personal Identity Verification-compliant credentials are accepted and electronically verified.</p>
          <link rel="assessment-for" href="#ia-2.12_smt"/>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.12_asm-examine" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="EXAMINE"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(12)-Examine"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Identification and authentication policy</p>
            <p>system security plan</p>
            <p>procedures addressing user identification and authentication</p>
            <p>system design documentation</p>
            <p>system configuration settings and associated documentation</p>
            <p>system audit records</p>
            <p>PIV verification records</p>
            <p>evidence of PIV credentials</p>
            <p>PIV credential authorizations</p>
            <p>other relevant documents or records</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.12_asm-interview" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="INTERVIEW"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(12)-Interview"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Organizational personnel with system operations responsibilities</p>
            <p>organizational personnel with account management responsibilities</p>
            <p>organizational personnel with information security responsibilities</p>
            <p>system/network administrators</p>
            <p>system developers</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.12_asm-test" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="TEST"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(12)-Test"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Mechanisms supporting and/or implementing acceptance and verification of PIV credentials</p>
          </part>
        </part>
      </control>
      <control class="SP800-53-enhancement" id="ia-2.13">
        <title>Out-of-band Authentication</title>
        <param id="ia-02.13_odp.01">
          <prop name="alt-identifier" value="ia-2.13_prm_2"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(13)_ODP[01]"/>
          <label>out-of-band authentication</label>
          <guideline>
            <p>out-of-band authentication mechanisms to be implemented are defined;</p>
          </guideline>
        </param>
        <param id="ia-02.13_odp.02">
          <prop name="alt-identifier" value="ia-2.13_prm_1"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(13)_ODP[02]"/>
          <label>conditions</label>
          <guideline>
            <p>conditions under which out-of-band authentication is to be implemented are defined;</p>
          </guideline>
        </param>
        <prop name="label" class="zero-padded" value="IA-02(13)"/>
        <prop name="label" value="IA-2(13)"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(13)"/>
        <prop name="sort-id" value="ia-02.13"/>
        <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="implementation-level" value="system"/>
        <link rel="required" href="#ia-2"/>
        <link rel="related" href="#ia-10"/>
        <link rel="related" href="#ia-11"/>
        <link rel="related" href="#sc-37"/>
        <part name="statement" id="ia-2.13_smt">
          <p>Implement the following out-of-band authentication mechanisms under <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-02.13_odp.02"/>: <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-02.13_odp.01"/>.</p>
        </part>
        <part name="guidance" id="ia-2.13_gdn">
          <p>Out-of-band authentication refers to the use of two separate communication paths to identify and authenticate users or devices to an information system. The first path (i.e., the in-band path) is used to identify and authenticate users or devices and is generally the path through which information flows. The second path (i.e., the out-of-band path) is used to independently verify the authentication and/or requested action. For example, a user authenticates via a notebook computer to a remote server to which the user desires access and requests some action of the server via that communication path. Subsequently, the server contacts the user via the user’s cell phone to verify that the requested action originated from the user. The user may confirm the intended action to an individual on the telephone or provide an authentication code via the telephone. Out-of-band authentication can be used to mitigate actual or suspected <q>man-in the-middle</q> attacks. The conditions or criteria for activation include suspicious activities, new threat indicators, elevated threat levels, or the impact or classification level of information in requested transactions.</p>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.13_obj" name="assessment-objective">
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(13)"/>
          <p><insert type="param" id-ref="ia-02.13_odp.01"/> mechanisms are implemented under <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-02.13_odp.02"/>.</p>
          <link rel="assessment-for" href="#ia-2.13_smt"/>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.13_asm-examine" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="EXAMINE"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(13)-Examine"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Identification and authentication policy</p>
            <p>system security plan</p>
            <p>procedures addressing user identification and authentication</p>
            <p>system design documentation</p>
            <p>system configuration settings and associated documentation</p>
            <p>system audit records</p>
            <p>system-generated list of out-of-band authentication paths</p>
            <p>other relevant documents or records</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.13_asm-interview" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="INTERVIEW"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(13)-Interview"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Organizational personnel with system operations responsibilities</p>
            <p>organizational personnel with account management responsibilities</p>
            <p>organizational personnel with information security responsibilities</p>
            <p>system/network administrators</p>
            <p>system developers</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-2.13_asm-test" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="TEST"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-02(13)-Test"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Mechanisms supporting and/or implementing out-of-band authentication capability</p>
          </part>
        </part>
      </control>
    </control>
    <control class="SP800-53" id="ia-3">
      <title>Device Identification and Authentication</title>
      <param id="ia-03_odp.01">
        <prop name="alt-identifier" value="ia-3_prm_1"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-03_ODP[01]"/>
        <label>devices and/or types of devices</label>
        <guideline>
          <p>devices and/or types of devices to be uniquely identified and authenticated before establishing a connection are defined;</p>
        </guideline>
      </param>
      <param id="ia-03_odp.02">
        <prop name="alt-identifier" value="ia-3_prm_2"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-03_ODP[02]"/>
        <select how-many="one-or-more">
          <choice>local</choice>
          <choice>remote</choice>
          <choice>network</choice>
        </select>
      </param>
      <prop name="label" class="zero-padded" value="IA-03"/>
        <prop name="label" value="IA-3"/>
      <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-03"/>
      <prop name="sort-id" value="ia-03"/>
      <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="implementation-level" value="system"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#ac-17"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#ac-18"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#ac-19"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#au-6"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#ca-3"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#ca-9"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#ia-4"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#ia-5"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#ia-9"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#ia-11"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#ia-13"/>
      <link rel="related" href="#si-4"/>
      <part name="statement" id="ia-3_smt">
        <p>Uniquely identify and authenticate <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-03_odp.01"/> before establishing a <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-03_odp.02"/> connection.</p>
      </part>
      <part name="guidance" id="ia-3_gdn">
        <p>Devices that require unique device-to-device identification and authentication are defined by type, device, or a combination of type and device. Organization-defined device types include devices that are not owned by the organization. Systems use shared known information (e.g., Media Access Control [MAC], Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol [TCP/IP] addresses) for device identification or organizational authentication solutions (e.g., Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) 802.1x and Extensible Authentication Protocol [EAP], RADIUS server with EAP-Transport Layer Security [TLS] authentication, Kerberos) to identify and authenticate devices on local and wide area networks. Organizations determine the required strength of authentication mechanisms based on the security categories of systems and mission or business requirements. Because of the challenges of implementing device authentication on a large scale, organizations can restrict the application of the control to a limited number/type of devices based on mission or business needs.</p>
      </part>
      <part id="ia-3_obj" name="assessment-objective">
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-03"/>
        <p><insert type="param" id-ref="ia-03_odp.01"/> are uniquely identified and authenticated before establishing a <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-03_odp.02"/> connection.</p>
        <link rel="assessment-for" href="#ia-3_smt"/>
      </part>
      <part id="ia-3_asm-examine" name="assessment-method">
        <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="EXAMINE"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-03-Examine"/>
        <part name="assessment-objects">
          <p>Identification and authentication policy</p>
          <p>system security plan</p>
          <p>procedures addressing device identification and authentication</p>
          <p>system design documentation</p>
          <p>list of devices requiring unique identification and authentication</p>
          <p>device connection reports</p>
          <p>system configuration settings and associated documentation</p>
          <p>other relevant documents or records</p>
        </part>
      </part>
      <part id="ia-3_asm-interview" name="assessment-method">
        <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="INTERVIEW"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-03-Interview"/>
        <part name="assessment-objects">
          <p>Organizational personnel with operational responsibilities for device identification and authentication</p>
          <p>organizational personnel with information security responsibilities</p>
          <p>system/network administrators</p>
          <p>system developers</p>
        </part>
      </part>
      <part id="ia-3_asm-test" name="assessment-method">
        <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="TEST"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-03-Test"/>
        <part name="assessment-objects">
          <p>Mechanisms supporting and/or implementing device identification and authentication capabilities</p>
        </part>
      </part>
      <control class="SP800-53-enhancement" id="ia-3.1">
        <title>Cryptographic Bidirectional Authentication</title>
        <param id="ia-03.01_odp.01">
          <prop name="alt-identifier" value="ia-3.1_prm_1"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-03(01)_ODP[01]"/>
          <label>devices and/or types of devices</label>
          <guideline>
            <p>devices and/or types of devices requiring use of cryptographically based, bidirectional authentication to authenticate before establishing one or more connections are defined;</p>
          </guideline>
        </param>
        <param id="ia-03.01_odp.02">
          <prop name="alt-identifier" value="ia-3.1_prm_2"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-03(01)_ODP[02]"/>
          <select how-many="one-or-more">
            <choice>local</choice>
            <choice>remote</choice>
            <choice>network</choice>
          </select>
        </param>
        <prop name="label" class="zero-padded" value="IA-03(01)"/>
        <prop name="label" value="IA-3(1)"/>
        <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-03(01)"/>
        <prop name="sort-id" value="ia-03.01"/>
        <prop ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" name="implementation-level" value="system"/>
        <link rel="required" href="#ia-3"/>
        <link rel="related" href="#sc-8"/>
        <link rel="related" href="#sc-12"/>
        <link rel="related" href="#sc-13"/>
        <part name="statement" id="ia-3.1_smt">
          <p>Authenticate <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-03.01_odp.01"/> before establishing <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-03.01_odp.02"/> connection using bidirectional authentication that is cryptographically based.</p>
        </part>
        <part name="guidance" id="ia-3.1_gdn">
          <p>A local connection is a connection with a device that communicates without the use of a network. A network connection is a connection with a device that communicates through a network. A remote connection is a connection with a device that communicates through an external network. Bidirectional authentication provides stronger protection to validate the identity of other devices for connections that are of greater risk.</p>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-3.1_obj" name="assessment-objective">
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-03(01)"/>
          <p><insert type="param" id-ref="ia-03.01_odp.01"/> are authenticated before establishing <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-03.01_odp.02"/> connection using bidirectional authentication that is cryptographically based.</p>
          <link rel="assessment-for" href="#ia-3.1_smt"/>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-3.1_asm-examine" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="EXAMINE"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-03(01)-Examine"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Identification and authentication policy</p>
            <p>system security plan</p>
            <p>procedures addressing device identification and authentication</p>
            <p>system design documentation</p>
            <p>list of devices requiring unique identification and authentication</p>
            <p>device connection reports</p>
            <p>system configuration settings and associated documentation</p>
            <p>other relevant documents or records</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-3.1_asm-interview" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="INTERVIEW"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-03(01)-Interview"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">
            <p>Organizational personnel with operational responsibilities for device identification and authentication</p>
            <p>organizational personnel with information security responsibilities</p>
            <p>system/network administrators</p>
            <p>system developers</p>
          </part>
        </part>
        <part id="ia-3.1_asm-test" name="assessment-method">
          <prop name="method" ns="http://csrc.nist.gov/ns/rmf" value="TEST"/>
          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-03(01)-Test"/>
          <part name="assessment-objects">

          <prop name="label" class="sp800-53a" value="IA-03(03)_ODP[02]"/>

            <p>Where addresses are allocated dynamically, standardize dynamic address allocation lease information and the lease duration assigned to devices in accordance with <insert type="param" id-ref="ia-3.3_prm_1"/> ; and</p>
          </part>

        <part name="guidance" id="ia-3.3_gdn">
